Purvin & Gertz, Inc. in association with Levelton Consultants Ltd. (2004). Economic and Environmental Impacts of Removing Sulphur from Canadian Gasoline and Distillate Production. Prepared for the Canadian Petroleum Products Institute, Natural Resources Canada, Environment Canada and Industry Canada. G.R. Crandall and B.T. Crutcher. Project C-2435, August 4, 2004. Includes Levelton report (File 404-0022).

Region: Canada (Quebec/Atlantic, Ontario, Western Canada), refinery survey 2003-2004, constant 2003 CAD. Locators are the report's printed section-page numbers (IV-3, V-12); the landscape tables V-1 to V-5 have unreliable page headers, so their PDF page is given too. Loaded: for 8 region x desulphurization step combinations (gasoline 30 ppm, diesel 15 ppm, furnace oil 1000 ppm), incremental capex per m3/d and opex per m3 of desulphurized product, incremental fuel (HHV) and electricity per m3, and incremental CO2e per m3; all derived by the extractor from printed regional totals divided by printed product volumes (x365). Plus SMR feedstock and fuel CO2 factors per MMscf H2. No unit-level hydrotreater or hydrogen plant capacity/cost is printed (refinery data confidential), so no per-unit capex. TRAPS: (1) Table V-1 Electricity TJ row disagrees with its MWh row (e.g. diesel 4,864 TJ vs 181,338 MWh = 653 TJ); MWh used. (2) Hydrogen feedstock gas is non-fuel and excluded from fuel SEC; given as flows. (3) Volumes are refiners' desulphurized throughput, not unit capacity; incremental steps bundle hydrotreaters, hydrogen plants, sulphur plants. (4) Western Canada "other" fuel and refinery-fuel-gas feed reductions not loaded. Whole-refinery regional totals in other-values only.
